title: Your first hunt
summary: Build a reliable hunting routine before chasing damage numbers.

sections.title: Start in the training area
sections.text: Try the whole weapon roster before settling. The weapon that lets you read the monster and recover safely will outperform a fashionable build you cannot control.
bullets: Learn an approach, a short punish, and a safe exit.
Practice sheathing and item use; those are part of your moveset.
Use move names in this guide; consult the in-game control list for your platform.

sections.title: Prepare, observe, punish
sections.text: Eat, restock, and sharpen before leaving camp. Watch one attack without trying to trade into it, then hit the recovery. A monster turning toward you often signals that your next opening is ending.
bullets: Keep the monster and an escape route in view.
Spend long knockdowns on your weapon’s strongest reliable sequence.
After a faint, restore food or item buffs and restock rather than rushing back.

title: Capture or slay?
summary: Know the capture conditions and the targets that must be slain.

sections.title: The capture sequence
sections.text: A capturable monster must be sufficiently weakened, tranquilized, and held by a valid trap. A limp or a research-dependent skull indicator can help, but neither is a universal substitute for checking the hunt objective.
bullets: Bring a Shock Trap or Pitfall Trap and Tranq Bombs.
Two nearby Tranq Bombs are the usual preparation; you can tranquilize before trapping.
If it escapes a trap, damage or tranquilizer buildup may be insufficient.

sections.title: Exceptions matter
sections.text: Elder Dragons cannot be captured. Other exceptions include Leshen, Ancient Leshen, and Raging Brachydios. Some monsters also resist particular traps depending on their state.
bullets: Follow “capture” objectives exactly; killing the target fails them.
Check the monster profile before spending your traps.
Trap duration diminishes with repeated use during a hunt.

title: Quests, investigations & expeditions
summary: Choose the quest type that moves your goal forward.

sections.title: Use the right board entry
sections.text: Assigned quests advance the story. Optional quests unlock facilities, tools, and other practical rewards. Investigations are useful for targeted materials, with bonus reward boxes and their own conditions.
bullets: Read the time limit, faint limit, and player limit before departure.
A material’s reward chances depend on rank, quest, and part objective.
Gather tracks and reports to build your investigation options.

sections.title: Use expeditions deliberately
sections.text: Expeditions are useful for exploration, camp discovery, gathering, and ecological research. Roaming monsters can leave, so a proper quest is usually more predictable when farming a specific target.
bullets: Unlock camps; travel time is part of every hunt.
Turn in deliveries that complete discovered camps.
Check the Resource Center for bounties and deliveries between quests.

title: Damage, affinity & sharpness
summary: Understand the parts of a build that actually convert into damage.

sections.title: Read beyond the attack number
sections.text: Displayed attack uses weapon-specific scaling, so it is not a fair comparison between different weapon classes. Affinity is your chance to critically hit; negative affinity can produce weak hits.
bullets: Match the damage type and hitzone to your weapon.
A skill that is active only occasionally is not permanent damage.
Element and status are different systems; Blast is not an element.

sections.title: Keep the edge working
sections.text: Sharpness affects damage and whether many melee attacks bounce. Preserve usable sharpness with a suitable weapon, sharpening windows, and sharpness-management skills.
bullets: Handicraft does not add sharpness to every weapon.
Mind’s Eye can prevent certain bounces, but does not make a hard part a good damage target.
Critical Boost improves the physical critical multiplier; elemental critical damage needs the relevant set bonus or skill.

title: Build skills with a purpose
summary: Choose survival, uptime, and weapon skills before filling leftover slots.

sections.title: A practical priority order
sections.text: Start with the skills that keep your weapon functional and your hunter alive. Add affinity and damage when you can consistently reach the correct part.
bullets: Health Boost is a strong comfort investment before special endgame set bonuses.
Use weapon essentials: stamina support, Focus, Guard, ammo skills, or capacity where appropriate.
Choose resistance skills for a particular threat, rather than stacking defense blindly.

sections.title: Read skill levels and conditions
sections.text: Skill names alone do not tell the whole story. Some effects have caps, some require a set bonus to extend, and some only apply to a subset of attacks.
bullets: Weakness Exploit depends on suitable hitzones; current versions reward wounded weak parts further.
Raw-critical skills do not raise fixed shelling damage.
Use the in-game status and skill screens to verify your equipped result.

title: Item loadouts & radial menu
summary: Turn preparation into a quick, repeatable habit.

sections.title: Save two loadouts
sections.text: Keep a general hunting pouch and a gathering pouch. Save useful radial-menu shortcuts alongside item loadouts, and verify that crafting shortcuts use the quantities you expect.
bullets: General: healing, status cures, traps where valid, buffs, and utility.
Ranged: ammo or coatings plus ingredients for the ammunition you actually shoot.
Gathering: tools and space for the route, with an escape option.

sections.title: Restock after every hunt
sections.text: Returning with half a pouch is a preparation problem you can solve at the item box. Cultivate common ingredients and spend fewer quests gathering emergency supplies.
bullets: Carry crafting materials when the hunt may exceed your starting supply.
Set auto-crafting intentionally; do not consume scarce ingredients accidentally.
A Farcaster can save a difficult situation when the quest allows it.

title: Canteen, buffs & stamina
summary: Leave camp ready to hunt, and rebuild your buffs after a faint.

sections.title: Choose food for the hunt
sections.text: Meals can provide health, stamina, stat bonuses, and food skills. Fresh ingredients and the selected platter affect what you receive; a voucher helps activate food skills.
bullets: Read the actual meal effects rather than selecting only by appearance.
Use the canteen before the first engagement when possible.
After fainting, restore lost health and stamina capacity with the appropriate items.

sections.title: Stack carefully
sections.text: Some buffs coexist and others replace one another. Check your status screen instead of assuming every food or consumable increases a separate multiplier.
bullets: Use a Max Potion to restore health and raise maximum health.
Rations or Well-done Steak help recover stamina capacity.
Cold and hot areas may require drinks unless your equipment provides the needed protection.

title: Blights, ailments & cures
summary: Treat the condition that is costing you control or damage.

sections.title: Blights and ailments are different
sections.text: Nulberries remove elemental blights, including Dragonblight, which can shut down elemental and status output. Poison, bleeding, sleep, and effluvial health reduction use different answers.
bullets: Poison: Antidote or the quicker Herbal Medicine.
Bleeding: crouch safely to recover, or use Astera Jerky.
Effluvial health reduction: Nulberry; Effluvia Resistance prevents the buildup at sufficient levels.

sections.title: Prevent the next interruption
sections.text: A cure gets you through the current mistake; a resistance skill can protect a whole attempt. A specific counter often provides more real uptime than another offensive decoration.
bullets: Use an Adamant Seed to clear Defense Down.
Roll to help clear fireblight or blast buildup when the situation permits.
Sleep Resistance and Stun Resistance solve different threats.

title: Your Palico & field allies
summary: Make your companion a deliberate part of the plan.

sections.title: Choose a gadget for the problem
sections.text: Vigorwasp Spray helps with recovery; Coral Orchestra supplies buffs; Flashfly Cage controls suitable targets; Shieldspire draws attention; Plunderblade helps material collection; Meowlotov Cocktail adds damage.
bullets: Build relationships with local Grimalkynes to unlock gadgets and field support.
A Palico weapon can contribute status buildup even when you prioritize your own damage.
Check gadget proficiency and manual gadget commands.

sections.title: Plan around multiplayer
sections.text: Your Palico does not accompany a full four-hunter party. A solo strategy that relies on its distraction or status may behave differently when you join others.
bullets: Use the training and field environment to practice without relying on constant aggro relief.
Avoid assuming every hunt has a Vigorwasp revive available.
Change gadget according to the objective, not just your last hunt.

title: Mantles, boosters & slinger
summary: Use tools to create good decisions, rather than to force bad trades.

sections.title: Specialized tools
sections.text: Mantles and boosters are unlocked through progression and optional tasks. Their cooldowns and durations matter; remove a spent mantle when appropriate so its recovery can begin.
bullets: Temporal Mantle is not immunity to every form of damage.
Rocksteady can let repeated hits damage you without the usual knockback.
Health Booster is strongest when you can safely stay inside its area.

sections.title: Use the environment
sections.text: The slinger can interact with environmental traps, interrupt certain actions, and manipulate some monsters. Ammo types have different uses and are not interchangeable.
bullets: Learn falling-boulder and vine-trap locations.
Dung Pods can help separate unwanted monsters.
Flash Pods lose much of their reliability against resistant or repeatedly flashed targets.

title: Multiplayer that helps the hunt
summary: Coordinate objectives, positioning, and quest access.

sections.title: Before the SOS
sections.text: Some story assignments require each player to see a cutscene before others can join. Confirm the quest rank, password or session, and target before preparing a group.
bullets: The faint allowance is shared in most ordinary quests.
Use Flinch Free when teammate interruptions are a recurring problem.
Place long or explosive attacks so they do not repeatedly disrupt others.

sections.title: During the hunt
sections.text: Call out captures, sleep, and special mechanics. When a monster sleeps, coordinate the first strong wake-up hit and avoid an accidental low-value tap.
bullets: Bring team recovery when it supports the plan; it does not replace normal attacks.
Leave the best knockout access to teammates who need the head when practical.
Check platform compatibility; do not assume cross-platform play.

title: Defender & Guardian gear
summary: Decide whether you want a shortcut or the original learning curve.

sections.title: What the gear is for
sections.text: Defender weapons and Guardian armor are designed to accelerate progression toward Iceborne. They can make early encounters much more forgiving and reduce the need to learn normal upgrade choices.
bullets: Use them when you intentionally want to move through World quickly.
For a first playthrough, ordinary gear makes damage, positioning, and crafting decisions more visible.
A shortcut through High Rank does not remove the need to prepare for Master Rank.

sections.title: Keep learning either way
sections.text: Whichever gear you use, learn a reliable punish and how to leave an attack safely. Armor can absorb a mistake without explaining why it happened.
bullets: Try hunts without excessive defensive cushioning if you need to diagnose bad habits.
Learn capture, item shortcuts, and optional unlocks before the expansion.
Do not mistake a powerful weapon for a finished build.

title: After the World story
summary: Choose a High Rank goal instead of grinding without a target.

sections.title: Strengthen a coherent build
sections.text: Finish useful optional unlocks, improve armor, and investigate tempered monsters. Decorations and High Rank augment materials come from different reward systems; identify the one your build needs.
bullets: Prioritize suitable weapon stats and the skills you can consistently activate.
High Rank weapon augmentation differs from Iceborne’s Master Rank system.
Arch-tempered quests and collaboration fights require their own preparation.

sections.title: Special encounters
sections.text: High Rank Kulve Taroth is a siege with its own reward loop. Behemoth and Ancient Leshen are special collaboration encounters, with mechanics beyond an ordinary capture hunt.
bullets: Check availability in the game rather than relying on an old event calendar.
Drachen and other powerful sets require tackling their associated content.
If moving into Iceborne, early Master Rank armor will soon change your equipment priorities.

title: Clutch Claw & wall bangs
summary: Wound good targets and turn safe openings into knockdowns.

sections.title: Wounding and the flinch shot
sections.text: Clutch onto a suitable part during a safe opening. A weapon attack can wound a part; a flinch shot from the head can send a non-enraged monster into an obstacle when you have usable slinger ammo.
bullets: Use the long stagger opening often called a clagger.
Check the monster’s enrage state before attempting a wall bang.
Claw turns consume part of your opportunity; do not rotate endlessly.

sections.title: Weapon differences
sections.text: Weapons differ in how quickly their clutch attacks wound and whether they drop slinger ammo. Clutch Claw Boost helps bridge those differences in the current game.
bullets: A wounded part is valuable only if you and the team can keep hitting it.
Rocksteady and Temporal can help an attach, but neither guarantees safety.
Do not sacrifice repeated faints to maintain a wound during a dangerous move.

title: The Guiding Lands
summary: Farm the material and region you need, with a clear unlock plan.

sections.title: A different material loop
sections.text: The Guiding Lands opens after Iceborne’s main story. Its regional levels influence which monsters appear and whether they are tempered. Many dropped materials here are specific to this area and are used for augmentation.
bullets: Pick up shinies during safe openings.
Geologist can allow extra pickups from many relevant monster drops.
Use lures for a target you need and consult the in-game regional list.

sections.title: Rank gates and region management
sections.text: The MR 49, 69, and 99 assignments raise the practical progression gates. Completing the MR 99 assignment opens access to the highest regional level. Raising one region can lower others, so choose a plan before pushing everything.
bullets: Fix region levels when you want them to stay stable.
Join another hunter’s regions when that saves rebuilding your own.
Rarity and augmentation type determine which materials your weapon needs.

title: Master Rank augmentation
summary: Make the augment fit the weapon and the material cost.

sections.title: Read the actual recipe
sections.text: Augment slots, material requirements, and availability depend on weapon rarity and the chosen augmentation. Guiding Lands materials are central, but one popular recipe does not apply to every weapon.
bullets: Health regeneration behaves differently with rapid multi-hit attacks and ranged patterns.
Affinity augments can help complete a conditional affinity target.
Custom upgrades and regular augments are separate systems, and not every weapon supports both.

sections.title: Farm backward from the smithy
sections.text: Open the augment menu, identify the missing material, then locate its monster and regional requirement. This is more efficient than collecting random endgame materials.
bullets: Keep separate target lists for weapon augments and armor upgrades.
Revisit decoration and skill balance after changing an augment.
Consult the linked database for exact current material recipes.

title: Safi’jiiva & Kulve Taroth
summary: Treat these as separate reward systems, not interchangeable dragon farms.

sections.title: Safi’jiiva
sections.text: The recon teaches the encounter; the siege supplies the main awakened-weapon reward loop. Coordinate part breaks, environmental opportunities, and the encounter’s area mechanics.
bullets: Awakened abilities use their own upgrade resource and selection process.
Choose a weapon worth investing in before spending heavily.
Supercritical phases create opportunities, but require disciplined positioning.

sections.title: Master Rank Kulve Taroth
sections.text: The Master Rank quest is a slay hunt, distinct from the High Rank siege. Its materials can upgrade eligible appraisal weapons, while obtaining and improving those weapons involves their associated systems.
bullets: Read the current in-game availability for both encounters.
Kjárr weapons are notable for their built-in critical elemental or status-related skills.
Gold mantle and exposed phases can change your elemental priorities.

title: Alatreon: prepare for the elemental check
summary: Bring the correct element, maintain it, and learn the phase cycle.

sections.title: Before you depart
sections.text: A Fire Active start calls for an Ice weapon; an Ice Active start calls for Fire. The quest determines the starting state, so check it instead of assuming every Alatreon hunt is identical.
bullets: Blast and Poison do not satisfy the elemental suppression check.
Use actual elemental damage, not an element locked behind an inactive skill.
Dragonblight must be cleared or prevented to keep your elemental output working.

sections.title: During the cycle
sections.text: Elemental damage can weaken Escaton Judgement. Horn breaks are available during Dragon Active and influence the next elemental state; they do not replace the suppression check.
bullets: Aim for elemental buildup on suitable parts and learn the head openings.
Heal through a successfully weakened judgement with the correct timing.
Treat horn control and elemental suppression as two related objectives.

title: Fatalis: build for the attempt
summary: Survive the patterns, use the arena, and earn reliable head openings.

sections.title: Preparation
sections.text: The quest’s entry rank is not a guarantee of readiness. Upgrade your armor, prepare an appropriate build, and learn the arena tools. Partbreaker can help with head-break goals, but skill slots still need a coherent plan.
bullets: A fire-resistant number does not remove physical damage from attacks.
Use the openings you can reliably punish instead of chasing every head movement.
Review siege-weapon opportunities and reserve binders for useful moments.

sections.title: The hunt
sections.text: Head breaks matter for the later threat level. Learn the fire-cone positioning, phase transitions, and safe routes to the designated shelters.
bullets: Read the arena and transition messages.
Position a cone punish so you still have time to leave.
Make each attempt answer one question: which attack or transition caused the faint?

title: Entering Master Rank
summary: Replace the weakest parts of your High Rank setup early.

sections.title: Unlock the expansion
sections.text: Own Iceborne, complete World’s main campaign, and reach HR 16. Speak to the Feisty Fiver in Astera to begin the expedition into the expansion.
bullets: Follow the opening assignments into Hoarfrost Reach and Seliana.
Master Rank armor provides a useful defense step even before you perfect skills.
Keep a sensible weapon upgrade rather than spending heavily on a set you will replace immediately.

sections.title: A new rhythm
sections.text: Monsters become faster and less forgiving. Learn the Clutch Claw and your weapon’s new move, then rebuild your familiar hunting loop around the new openings.
bullets: Hot Drinks or suitable protection help with the cold.
Craft fresh item and equipment loadouts for the new rank.
The first story clear is the beginning of Iceborne’s longer endgame.

title: Mounting, knockdowns & control
summary: Create an opening, then spend it well.

sections.title: Different kinds of control
sections.text: Mounting buildup comes from appropriate aerial attacks. Stuns come from suitable blunt or stun-capable attacks to the head. Trips, part breaks, traps, and environmental knockdowns follow their own rules.
bullets: An aerial attack is not automatically your best damage choice.
A monster can become more resistant to repeated control effects.
Do not confuse exhausting a monster with stunning it.

sections.title: Use the opening
sections.text: Have a planned sequence for a full knockdown and a shorter sequence for a small stagger. Sharpening or healing can be the right choice when the next mistake would end the quest.
bullets: Reposition before committing a long combo.
If a teammate mounts, use the time to prepare rather than wasting a trap at random.
Avoid combining every control tool at once if sequential use would give more useful openings.

title: Research, small monsters & endemic life
summary: The ecosystem is useful even when it is not your quest target.

sections.title: Research and small monsters
sections.text: Collect tracks, investigate behavior, and report to the Ecological Research team. Small monsters supply specific crafting materials and can interrupt a hunt, so treat them as part of the route.
bullets: Aptonoth, Apceros, and other herbivores are not large-monster boss hunts.
Wingdrakes, insects, and scavengers can have valuable materials.
Consult the exact material entry when you need a rank-specific drop.

sections.title: Endemic life
sections.text: Use the capture net for eligible endemic creatures, rather than treating them like carve targets. Weather, time, and location can influence rare appearances.
bullets: A ghillie approach helps with easily startled creatures.
Check bounties from the relevant researchers.
The fishing rod and capture net solve different collection tasks.

title: Botanical Research & resource loops
summary: Grow the ingredients that keep your chosen loadout supplied.

sections.title: Cultivate deliberately
sections.text: The cultivation system turns unlocked ingredients into a steady supply. Complete its optional unlocks and keep fertilizer effects maintained where appropriate.
bullets: Prioritize Honey and the ingredients you actually consume.
Ranged hunters should budget for ammo ingredients.
Do not let a full harvest box waste a cultivation cycle.

sections.title: Make each hunt do more
sections.text: Register bounties that align with your plan, use investigations for the target material, and check deliveries after a session.
bullets: A focused material goal is usually more useful than random crafting.
Keep a small reserve for traps and status cures.
Upgrade facilities as part of progression; they repay the time over many hunts.

title: Read the part, not just the weakness stars
summary: Choose a reachable target using physical and elemental hitzones separately.

sections.title: Two different matchups
sections.text: A monster's best cutting, blunt and shot targets can differ. Elemental hitzones are another set of values, so a part that takes strong physical damage is not automatically the best elemental target.
bullets: Read the correct damage column for your attack.
Check alternate states such as broken armour, mud coatings or charged parts.
A higher hitzone value means that part accepts more of that damage type.

sections.title: Turn the numbers into a plan
sections.text: Pick a reliable target while the monster is moving, then a stronger target for a knockdown. Repeated clean hits on an accessible part can beat chasing the head and missing every opening.
bullets: Practise approaching the same side after a familiar attack.
Use the monster database to compare the parts you can actually reach.

title: Guard, evade or leave the attack?
summary: Choose a defensive answer before committing to a long punish.

sections.title: A shield has a cost
sections.text: Blocking can consume stamina, cause knockback and allow chip damage. Shield strength and the incoming attack matter; equipping a shield does not make every attack safe to hold through.
bullets: Face the incoming hit and keep stamina available.
Guard improves blocking; Guard Up permits additional attack types rather than replacing Guard.
Some encounter mechanics still require a different answer.

sections.title: Create space deliberately
sections.text: An evade can move you out of a hitbox or pass through it with careful timing. Evade Extender changes travel distance, while Evade Window changes the invulnerability window. Test the resulting spacing with your weapon.
bullets: For a large attack, sheathing early can be safer than attempting a late dodge.
Practise one repeatable defensive response before extending the follow-up combo.

title: Ranged damage: stay in the useful range
summary: A connected shot can still be a poor shot if its range or target is wrong.

sections.title: Use the reticle
sections.text: Critical distance is a range mechanic, separate from affinity and critical hits. Suitable spacing depends on the ammunition or coating, so the distance that works for one setup may be wrong for another.
bullets: Watch the aiming reticle as you move toward or away from the target.
Pierce needs a useful path through the monster, not merely a hit on its nearest edge.
Close-range coating changes the bow's useful range.

sections.title: Keep an exit
sections.text: Stand where your next dodge leaves room to recover. A comfortable firing position should give you both a suitable hitzone and a route away from the next charge.
bullets: Recheck range after a knockdown moves the monster.
Evaluate damage with the ammunition, mods and skills you intend to use.

title: Part breaks, tail cuts and the material you need
summary: Plan a reward objective separately from simply finishing the hunt.

sections.title: Check the reward method
sections.text: A material can belong to a carve, capture, dropped-material, investigation or specific part-break pool. Read its rank and method before committing to a farming route.
bullets: A broken tail and a severed tail are different objectives.
Severable tails require suitable cutting damage; hitting the tail with any damage type is not enough.
Some special breaks have additional conditions.

sections.title: Control the finish
sections.text: If you need a particular break, attack that part during the safest long opening and communicate the objective in a group. Do not assume a capture replaces the reward from a break you never achieved.
bullets: Use the profile's breakability and reward tables together.
Pick up detached carves and safe dropped materials before leaving.

title: Enraged is not the same as exhausted
summary: Recognise why the monster's pace changed before choosing a control tool.

sections.title: Different systems
sections.text: Enrage can change aggression, attack sequences and other monster properties. Exhaustion concerns monster stamina. Neither is a universal low-health indicator, and a tired-looking monster is not automatically ready for capture.
bullets: Relearn the end of an attack chain when a monster enrages.
Do not confuse a stun or a trip with exhaustion.
Consult each monster's behaviour instead of expecting identical fatigue responses.

sections.title: Iceborne opportunity
sections.text: Flinch shots that send a monster into a wall generally require it to be out of enrage. Use the displayed state and a safe head opening rather than repeatedly clawing onto an already enraged target.
bullets: Save recovery time by abandoning a failed wall-bang setup early.
A shorter punish is sensible while learning an enraged follow-up.

title: Give each slinger pod a job
summary: Use environmental ammunition for interruption, distraction and route control.

sections.title: More than spare damage
sections.text: Slinger ammunition has different effects. Stones can trigger environmental objects, while other pods are useful for interrupting or distracting suitable targets. Read the loaded ammunition before relying on it.
bullets: Look for hanging traps and reachable slinger interactions before combat starts.
Do not spend every useful pod on random damage.
A distraction only helps if you use the opening to reposition or complete a task.

sections.title: Keep special pods ready
sections.text: Flash Pods, Dung Pods and Screamer Pods solve different problems. Flash Pods need appropriate positioning; Dung Pods may encourage an unwanted monster to leave; Screamer Pods only disrupt susceptible monsters in the right situation.
bullets: Monster state and resistance can change the result.
Restock the pod ingredients your usual hunt actually consumes.

title: Choose armour pieces, not just a matching outfit
summary: Compare skills, slots and set-bonus thresholds before crafting a whole set.

sections.title: Read each variant
sections.text: Alpha and beta versions can distribute innate skills and decoration slots differently. Later variants are separate records too. A beta piece is not automatically an upgrade if you lack decorations that make its slots useful.
bullets: Compare the actual skill levels and slot sizes.
Check the rank; similarly named sets can belong to different progression tiers.
A mixed set can combine useful pieces without preserving the visual outfit.

sections.title: Spend on a usable result
sections.text: Before crafting, total the skills your finished five-piece selection and charm provide. Preserve any set-bonus threshold the build needs, then use remaining slots for its missing functions.
bullets: Upgrade defence on equipment you will use.
Use layered armour when you want a different appearance without rebuilding the underlying set.

title: Decoration rarity is not slot size
summary: Read the jewel's required slot level and granted skill points separately.

sections.title: Fit the jewel
sections.text: A decoration occupies one compatible equipment slot. Its required slot level must not exceed that slot's level. The rarity value describes the decoration, not the number of slots it consumes.
bullets: A larger slot can hold a smaller required-slot decoration.
A level-four slot does not mean four separate jewels fit inside it.
Iceborne's combination decorations can grant two different skills, or multiple levels of one skill.

sections.title: Check the finished skill list
sections.text: Read the levels actually granted by the jewel; its name alone is not a complete build calculation. Keep valuable large slots available when smaller ones can hold the same utility jewel.
bullets: Avoid adding skill levels beyond an active cap.
Review decorations when changing a weapon, charm or armour piece.

title: Use the charm to finish the build
summary: One upgraded charm can replace several missing decoration requirements.

sections.title: Plan its upgrade path
sections.text: A charm is its own equipment piece. It supplies skills without occupying your armour's decoration slots, and many charms can be upgraded as their material requirements become available.
bullets: Compare the charm at the upgrade level you can actually craft.
Check whether a desired recipe needs a later rank or special material.
A utility charm can be useful while your decoration collection is small.

sections.title: Rebalance after an upgrade
sections.text: When the charm gains skill levels, remove duplicated decoration levels and use the space for another requirement. Save the complete result as an equipment loadout so a later hunt does not start with the wrong charm.
bullets: Keep alternate sets for different resistance or stamina needs.
Verify the equipped skills, not just the saved loadout's name.

title: Set bonuses and skill Secrets
summary: Unlocking a skill cap and filling that cap are separate steps.

sections.title: Count the qualifying pieces
sections.text: Set bonuses activate at their stated equipment thresholds. Read which pieces qualify and which effect each threshold grants. A strong individual piece may still be the wrong swap if removing it disables the bonus your build relies on.
bullets: Check the active bonus in the equipped skill list.
Different bonuses may share a theme without sharing the same qualifying set.
Do not assume every set requires all five armour pieces.

sections.title: Iceborne: the Secret is a raised limit
sections.text: A Secret effect permits higher levels of its associated skill. You still need equipment or decorations that supply those levels; unlocking the raised cap does not automatically fill it.
bullets: Compare the actual active level before and after changing pieces.
Keep conditional effects separate from permanently active stats.

title: Hidden element and status attributes
summary: A greyed-out attribute needs activation before it contributes to the hunt.

sections.title: Read the active state
sections.text: Some weapons show a hidden element or status attribute in parentheses. Free Elem/Ammo Up can release a hidden attribute, with the active amount depending on the skill level. Its ammunition effect is a separate use of the same skill.
bullets: Check the equipped status screen after changing the skill.
Do not select an elemental counter using an attribute that is still inactive.
An element and a status ailment are different systems.

sections.title: Choose a complete setup
sections.text: Compare the weapon with the skills needed to support it. Spending several slots to activate an attribute changes what you can fit elsewhere, so the highest printed elemental number is not a complete comparison.
bullets: Confirm the target's relevant elemental hitzones.
Recheck skills that depend on a weapon having no active element or status.

sources.name: MHWI — Free Elem/Ammo Up and Non-elemental Boost

title: Choose a bowgun around its ammunition
summary: Reload, recoil, magazine size and movement matter as much as displayed attack.

sections.title: Start with the shot you want
sections.text: Two bowguns with similar attack can handle the same ammunition very differently. Inspect the supported ammo table, recoil, reload and available modifications before crafting.
bullets: Choose the main ammunition before choosing the gun.
Check the effect of your fitted mods on that specific ammunition.
A rapid-fire option is not automatically the best option for every target.

sections.title: Practise the supply loop
sections.text: Save ammunition and its crafting materials in your item loadout. Test the radial crafting shortcut, then practise reloading during a safe opening instead of waiting until a charge forces an emergency reload.
bullets: Carry only support ammunition you can use effectively.
Keep enough space and materials for the full hunt.
A comfortable reload setup can produce more reliable damage than a fragile theoretical maximum.

title: Choose and maintain a Kinsect
summary: Your Kinsect has its own damage type, dust, speed and elemental choices.

sections.title: Read the separate equipment record
sections.text: Kinsects differ in attack type, dust effect, power, speed and healing-related attributes. Compare the Kinsect alongside the equipped glaive's Kinsect bonus rather than treating it as a cosmetic attachment.
bullets: A faster Kinsect can make distant extract collection more comfortable.
Severing and blunt Kinsects have different physical damage types.
Check the chosen element and dust effect in the equipment screen.

sections.title: Bring extracts back
sections.text: An extract only applies when the Kinsect returns it. Learn the target's extract locations and keep red extract available for the strengthened moveset. Marking a suitable part lets the Kinsect attack it and leave dust.
bullets: Recall before its stamina is exhausted when that helps your rhythm.
Dust remains where it was produced; the monster may move away.

title: Palico equipment has a separate job
summary: Choose the weapon's effect and the armour's protection independently of your gadget.

sections.title: Weapon, armour and gadget
sections.text: Your Palico's weapon, head armour, body armour and gadget are separate choices. Compare weapon damage type and any element or status, then keep its armour appropriate for the hunt's rank.
bullets: A status weapon can support your control plan without matching your hunter's element.
Choose the gadget for healing, distraction, control, materials or damage.
Higher-rank equipment has its own recipes; inspect the exact record.

sections.title: Plan around uncertain timing
sections.text: The Palico is helpful, but its next action is not a guaranteed on-demand opening. Treat an unexpected sleep or paralysis as a chance to stop, communicate and prepare a deliberate punish.
bullets: Reassess the plan when joining a party that removes your Palico.
Do not build a survival strategy around a rescue that may be unavailable.

title: Unlock the Palico's field gadgets
summary: Follow local Lynian requests instead of waiting for gadgets to appear at the smithy.

sections.title: Local friendships
sections.text: The base-game gadget unlocks are tied to the local Lynian groups: Bugtrappers in the Ancient Forest, Protectors in the Wildspire Waste, Troupers in the Coral Highlands, Plunderers in the Rotten Vale, and the Gajalaka request chain.
bullets: Look for the Lynian Researcher's requests and expedition opportunities.
Bring your Palico when working on field relationships.
Complete the local objective; simply finding a camp does not finish every unlock.

sections.title: Use what you unlocked
sections.text: Equip a gadget deliberately and build its proficiency through hunts. Higher proficiency expands what that gadget can do, while Iceborne adds further gadget development.
bullets: Check manual gadget commands when available.
Keep a material-gathering gadget and a survival gadget ready for different sessions.

title: Make Tailraider Safari part of the routine
summary: Choose a route for the materials it can return, then collect and dispatch between hunts.

sections.title: A route has a reward pool
sections.text: Safari routes show different encounters and gathering opportunities. Check the destination and rank before spending resources, especially when you need a safari-specific item.
bullets: Read the route's targets rather than selecting only by its length.
Match the team's useful abilities to the displayed route where possible.
Safari rewards supplement your hunts; they do not replace every rare-material source.

sections.title: Keep the cycle moving
sections.text: Check the returned haul during your normal base visit and send the next team before departure. Combine this with collecting cultivation and reviewing bounties so facility maintenance becomes one short stop.
bullets: Keep enough research points for the services you use.
Consult the safari reward list before repeatedly sending the wrong route.

sources.name: Kiranico — Tailraider Safari routes and rewards

title: Raider Ride: travel while preparing
summary: Use a local Tailraider as transport, with a destination rather than direct steering.

sections.title: Set the destination
sections.text: Raider Ride provides a mountable local Tailraider after the relevant local cooperation is unlocked. Set a map destination or follow a tracked monster; this is transport rather than a directly steered combat mount.
bullets: Check whether the locale's Raider Ride is available before relying on it.
Use the journey to prepare permitted items or equipment maintenance.
Dismount before the approach puts you into an unsafe attack.

sections.title: Different from a mounted topple
sections.text: The ride is separate from mounting a large monster through aerial attacks. It is also distinct from the Tailraider Signal that recruits field allies after its own unlock.
bullets: Keep the two tools separate in your shortcuts.
Unlocked camps remain useful for longer-distance travel.

sources.name: Capcom — Iceborne developer diary: Gathering Hub and field features

title: Pawswap and treasure tips
summary: Build local friendships and turn item trades into a separate exploration activity.

sections.title: Trading with local groups
sections.text: Pawswap becomes available through sufficient unity with the relevant Lynian group. Offer items and watch the group's reaction before committing to a trade; not every offered item is equally interesting to them.
bullets: Carry a few inexpensive options instead of your only rare consumable.
Collect the returned items and check for a new treasure tip.
Keep each locale's friendship and treasure progress separate.

sections.title: Follow the clue
sections.text: A treasure tip is a small exploration puzzle, rather than a normal gathering-node marker. Read its wording, inspect the suggested area and use your Palico's reactions to narrow the search.
bullets: Finish one clue chain before assuming the next clue is available.
Treat this as optional exploration, separate from required story progression.

title: Give the Argosy a useful order
summary: Request supplies, materials or trade-in goods according to your current shortage.

sections.title: Choose the cargo
sections.text: The Argosy brings cargo that you can purchase with research points. Its requested cargo categories serve different goals, so choose them around your supplies, crafting needs or money shortage.
bullets: Inspect the returned goods before buying them.
Trade-in goods are intended to be sold for zenny.
Keep research points available for cultivation, safaris and other services too.

sections.title: Use it as a supplement
sections.text: A random delivery is helpful background income, but an exact monster part is usually better pursued through its recorded source. Review cargo when the ship returns, then return to your chosen hunt rather than farming aimlessly.
bullets: Do not sell ordinary crafting materials just because they look plentiful.
Use the dedicated sell-trade-in-items option when clearing valuables.

sources.name: Monster Hunter World Chronicles — Argosy cargo

title: Steamworks: spend fuel with a purpose
summary: Use Seliana's supply minigame without sacrificing materials needed for your next upgrade.

sections.title: Fuel is a resource
sections.text: The Steamworks converts fuel into a range of rewards through its three-input sequence. Dedicated fuel materials are a useful source; inspect the conversion before feeding ordinary ores you still need for crafting.
bullets: Check the current reward display and overdrive bonus.
Festival-related reward changes are separate from normal crafting recipes.
Use any unlocked higher-output setting with its higher fuel consumption in mind.

sections.title: Avoid the guaranteed-drop assumption
sections.text: The facility is a supply source, not a promise that one fuel session gives a particular rare decoration. If you need a jewel, check which tickets, melding options or quest rewards can actually provide it.
bullets: Collect the rewards and return to the material goal that brought you to base.
Preserve a reserve for equipment you plan to craft.

sources.name: Capcom — Iceborne title update and Steamworks additions

title: The Elder Melder has several different systems
summary: Separate fixed exchanges, material melding and random appraisal pools before spending.

sections.title: Read the selected service
sections.text: Melding is not one universal recipe list. Some services exchange accepted materials for a chosen item, some use special prints, and others produce random rewards from a specific pool.
bullets: Check the output quantity, accepted inputs and required points.
A recipe being listed does not mean it is unlocked in your save.
Keep limited prints or tickets until their intended exchange is clear.

sections.title: Choose inputs carefully
sections.text: Spend surplus materials rather than the only copy needed for an upgrade. A random decoration-melding method cannot produce every jewel in the game; check its pool instead of assuming that more attempts solve an incompatible target.
bullets: Compare a direct exchange with the alternative hunt cost.
Revisit the menu after progression unlocks new services.

sources.name: Kiranico — Elder Melder recipes and pools

title: Bounties: earn rewards alongside your real goal
summary: Register tasks that your planned hunts will already complete.

sections.title: Pick compatible work
sections.text: Registered bounties can reward routine hunting and gathering. Select ones that overlap with your next material target, then collect completed rewards before replacing them.
bullets: Combine a monster-category bounty with the target you intend to hunt.
Gathering bounties fit naturally into a resource route.
A bounty is not an investigation and does not add investigation reward boxes.

sections.title: Check limited tasks separately
sections.text: Limited bounties have their own objectives and displayed reward conditions. Read the current in-game list rather than following an old daily or festival timetable.
bullets: Do not assume a task is complete before checking its rank and objective.
Armour-sphere rewards are useful only after you spend them upgrading equipment.

title: A discovered unlock may still need a delivery
summary: Check requests at the Resource Center when a camp or facility seems unfinished.

sections.title: Discovery is only the first step
sections.text: Some facility and camp upgrades require a delivery of materials and research points. Finding the location or speaking to an NPC can create the request without completing it.
bullets: Inspect pending deliveries after exploring a new locale.
Read the exact item rank and quantity.
Do not sell an item reserved for a useful facility unlock.

sections.title: Prioritise repeated value
sections.text: An extra camp, cultivation improvement or canteen ingredient can benefit many later hunts. Complete those requests when the materials are within reach, then verify that the unlocked service is actually usable.
bullets: Use the map to confirm newly available travel points.
Check NPC request markers after major story milestones.

title: Unlock more than the Chef's Choice
summary: Canteen ingredients come from requests and exploration, not only story progress.

sections.title: Build the ingredient list
sections.text: Additional ingredients expand your custom meal options. Their unlocks include quests, deliveries and gathering discoveries. Check the ingredient's recorded source rather than repeatedly eating and expecting the missing ingredient to appear.
bullets: Follow canteen-related NPC requests.
Some gathering discoveries depend on the locale's displayed resource condition.
An unlocked ingredient and a fresh ingredient are different properties.

sections.title: Choose the skill first
sections.text: Plan a custom platter around the food skill you want and inspect its activation chance. Iceborne's added drinks include useful exploration and preparation choices, including Felyne Zoomaster for rare endemic-life searches.
bullets: Read what the selected voucher changes before using it.
Save useful custom meals so the ingredients are easy to select again.

title: Farm backward from the missing material
summary: Find the right rank and reward method before choosing a quest.

sections.title: Read the exact record
sections.text: A scale, scale-plus, shard, gem and mantle can require different ranks and reward pools. Similar names do not make them interchangeable. Start with the missing ingredient, then inspect its listed sources.
bullets: Check body carves, capture, specific breaks and quest rewards separately.
Use an investigation whose bonus rewards suit the target.
Compare the quest's failure conditions with how reliably you can finish it.

sections.title: Count successful cycles
sections.text: A short hunt with consistent completion can be a better farming choice than a difficult quest you frequently fail. Include travel, restocking and reward collection when judging the route.
bullets: Set a material goal before departing.
Pick up safe drops during the fight.
Stop crafting side projects with the same scarce ingredient until the main upgrade is finished.

title: Build a short gathering circuit
summary: Link the nodes you need instead of sweeping the entire locale.

sections.title: Choose the correct nodes
sections.text: Mining outcrops, bonepiles, plants, insects and account-item gathering points have different pools. Match the material to its locale and rank, then connect a small number of useful areas.
bullets: Start from the closest unlocked camp.
Check the locale's current resource condition.
Leave room for the items you intend to collect.

sections.title: Use a gathering loadout
sections.text: Equip relevant gathering skills only when their effects apply to your route. Botanist, Geologist and Master Gatherer do different jobs; none should be assumed to duplicate every possible pickup.
bullets: Save a separate equipment and item loadout.
Keep an escape option when gathering around hostile monsters.
Cultivate renewable ingredients instead of gathering each potion's ingredients manually.

title: Read the map vertically
summary: A nearby icon can be on another floor, and a good camp can shorten every hunt.

sections.title: Check the layer
sections.text: Locales contain overlapping routes, tunnels and vertical connections. Before running directly toward a marker, check its layer and the route that connects your current area to it.
bullets: Use area numbers together with the visible elevation.
Learn one dependable route from each camp.
Use wedge beetles and other available traversal points where they shorten the journey.

sections.title: Unlock then use the camp
sections.text: Discovering a campsite may create a delivery request. Complete the request, then select that camp when posting suitable quests or travelling through the locale.
bullets: A nearer camp can save more time than a small damage increase.
The tent can help you restock and change equipment where the quest allows it.
Do not assume fast travel is available during every dangerous situation.

title: Search for rare endemic life systematically
summary: Use the creature's conditions and a quiet approach instead of repeating a blind circuit.

sections.title: Check the conditions
sections.text: Some creatures depend on particular places, times or weather. Read the individual entry before travelling, and distinguish those requirements from a creature simply being uncommon.
bullets: Keep the capture net ready before approaching.
Use a quiet approach for easily startled creatures.
A monster's absence does not guarantee a rare creature is present.

sections.title: Iceborne assistance
sections.text: Felyne Zoomaster makes rare endemic life more likely to appear, but does not guarantee the next spawn. Plan a route with several eligible checks and use failed visits for gathering or research along the way.
bullets: Confirm that the food skill actually activated.
Do not confuse endemic-life rarity or size with large-monster crowns.
Avoid treating an anecdotal spawn sighting as a universal rule.

sources.name: Monster Hunter Wiki — World endemic-life descriptions

title: Fishing is a useful supply route
summary: Learn a few fishing pools for useful fish, research requests and collection goals.

sections.title: Look before casting
sections.text: Different fish occupy different pools, and rare fish may have extra appearance conditions. Inspect the water and the target's entry instead of assuming every pond shares one reward pool.
bullets: Use the fishing rod for a deliberate catch.
Keep the net in mind for eligible nearby creatures, with its different approach requirements.
Follow the Piscine Researcher's requested species rather than catching random fish.

sections.title: Keep useful catches
sections.text: Fishing can contribute useful supplies as well as collection progress. Check the resulting item's function: some fish-related materials support healing, bombs or sharpening rather than ordinary monster-equipment recipes.
bullets: Carry what the route needs without filling the pouch with unrelated supplies.
Bookmark useful fishing locations alongside the item entry.

sources.name: Monster Hunter Wiki — Fish and endemic life in World

title: Surveyor Set: photograph the requested behaviour
summary: A research photograph needs the right subject, action and framing.

sections.title: Read all the criteria
sections.text: The Lynian Researcher's observation requests ask for specific scenes. A photograph of the right species can still miss the requested behaviour, subject size or direction.
bullets: Read the request before approaching its location.
Watch the scene long enough to recognise the requested action.
Frame the subject clearly and check the game's photograph feedback.

sections.title: Observe without interrupting
sections.text: Use a safe vantage point and avoid disturbing the scene while trying to improve the frame. Report suitable photographs to the researcher; keeping an image in the album alone is not the same as submitting the request.
bullets: Keep interesting unrelated pictures as a separate collection.
Treat each request as optional observation rather than a combat objective.

sources.name: Capcom — Surveyor Set and base updates

title: Large-monster crowns: size is a separate goal
summary: Choose eligible quests and record progress without confusing size with difficulty.

sections.title: Read the size record
sections.text: Large monsters can appear at different sizes, and qualifying small or large sizes are recorded separately in the Hunter's Notes. A monster looking unusually large is a useful clue, not an exact measurement.
bullets: Check whether your selected quest can produce the size you need.
A stronger or tempered monster is not automatically a crown-sized monster.
Fixed-size event quests and variable-size quests need different expectations.

sections.title: Make the hunt worthwhile
sections.text: Combine eligible crown attempts with useful materials or registered bounties. Keep a short list of missing species and sizes so you do not repeatedly farm a crown you already own.
bullets: Read achievement requirements separately from your personal full collection.
Confirm the recorded result after the hunt.

sources.name: Kiranico — Great Jagras size thresholds and quest records
Capcom — Master Rank event quest descriptions

title: A second monster can be an opportunity or a problem
summary: Use the interaction, then keep the target and your escape route clear.

sections.title: Watch the interaction
sections.text: Some monster pairs have specific turf-war animations; other encounters are ordinary overlapping attacks. Do not assume that every pair will perform a turf war or that the resulting damage finishes your objective.
bullets: Step clear of the interaction's attack area.
Use a safe moment to heal, sharpen or reposition.
Keep the actual quest target in view when the monsters separate.

sections.title: Separate when necessary
sections.text: An invader that blocks every opening can cost more than it contributes. Use suitable separation tools or move to a cleaner fighting area rather than trading into attacks from two directions.
bullets: Dung Pods are a tool, not a guarantee against every monster.
Avoid chasing both monsters into a narrow passage.
Preserve control tools for a usable opening rather than spending everything during the chaos.

title: Join the hunt with the right supplies
summary: Read the host's objective before treating every SOS as a standard slay quest.

sections.title: Before joining
sections.text: Check the target, rank, elapsed time and conditions. Bring the items your role needs rather than relying on a supply box that other hunters have already used.
bullets: Respect capture, part-break and special-mechanic objectives.
Leave shared supplies for teammates who need them.
If a story cutscene blocks joining, each player may need to reach the joinable point first.

sections.title: Coordinate a few important moments
sections.text: A short capture, sleep or binder callout is more useful than constant chat. Pause attacks when a deliberate wake-up or capture is being arranged, and give teammates room for their strongest punish.
bullets: Shared faint limits make a safe recovery valuable to everyone.
Team healing supports a plan; it does not require spending the whole hunt away from the monster.

title: Arena and Special Arena are different
summary: Check whether the quest uses preset equipment or your own build.

sections.title: The Arena Counter
sections.text: Arena quests at the Gathering Hub use selected preset weapon, armour and item loadouts. Their restrictions and time-based performance goals are part of the challenge, so your ordinary equipment build does not carry into them.
bullets: Inspect the supplied items before starting the fight.
Choose a preset you can use reliably.
Read the quest's own player and failure conditions.

sections.title: Optional Special Arena quests
sections.text: A Special Arena quest is a different type of quest using your own equipment. Capturing eligible monsters can unlock associated optional arena opportunities; it does not turn them into the preset-equipment Arena Counter challenge.
bullets: Check the exact quest title when farming a coin or completing optional quests.
Use the arena's available tools when they help the objective.

sources.name: Monster Hunter Wiki — World quest types

title: Guiding Lands: normal and tempered materials
summary: A familiar monster can have a different material pool here.

sections.title: Name the exact ingredient
sections.text: Guiding Lands materials are distinct from many ordinary quest rewards. Tempered versions of a monster can supply different materials from their non-tempered counterparts, so match the smithy's recipe to the exact entry.
bullets: Check the required regional level and monster state.
Pick up safe shinies throughout the encounter.
Mining and bonepile resources are separate from monster-specific drops.

sections.title: Use the regional tools
sections.text: Choose lures and regional goals around the next upgrade rather than raising a region without a target. Check the Elder Melder for unlocked material exchanges, but do not assume every required material can be exchanged immediately.
bullets: A friend's suitable region can save rebuilding your own.
Review materials before lowering a region you still need.

sources.name: Capcom — Guiding Lands region and material changes
Kiranico — Guiding Lands and exchange materials

title: Layered equipment changes the look
summary: Separate appearance recipes from the equipment supplying your combat stats.

sections.title: Keep the real build underneath
sections.text: Layered armour changes appearance while the equipped combat armour continues to provide defence, skills and decoration slots. Unlocking a layered appearance does not replace the need to craft and upgrade the equipment beneath it.
bullets: Read whether the smithy menu is showing combat or layered equipment.
Appearance recipes can require their own tickets or later-game materials.
Save the appearance with the appropriate loadout options.

sections.title: Iceborne weapon appearance
sections.text: Iceborne adds layered weapon options through its equipment systems. Eligible appearances and materials depend on the weapon and unlocks; changing the look is separate from choosing attack, element or sharpness.
bullets: Verify the combat record after changing equipment, not after judging its model.
Use appearance choices to keep a mixed armour set visually coherent.

sources.name: Capcom — Layered armour retains equipped stats and skills

title: Make the locale part of your punish
summary: Learn environmental traps before you need an emergency opening.

sections.title: Survey before the fight
sections.text: Boulders, vine traps and other environmental interactions can create damage or control opportunities. Look for their trigger and landing area while approaching, rather than discovering the interaction during a dangerous combo.
bullets: Stand where you can activate the trap without being caught in a charge.
Confirm the monster is actually inside the affected area.
Some environmental features have limited uses or require particular conditions.

sections.title: Prepare the follow-up
sections.text: An environmental topple is valuable when you are ready to reach a suitable part. If you are low on health or sharpness, using some of that opening to recover can make the rest of the hunt more stable.
bullets: Avoid overlapping every control effect unnecessarily.
Include useful trap locations in a familiar locale route.

title: Research levels and Scoutfly tracking
summary: Collect evidence and report research; a visible trail is not the whole system.

sections.title: Collect and report
sections.text: Tracks, traces and hunting activity contribute to monster research. Visit Ecological Research to review progress and the information available in the Hunter's Notes rather than leaving every update unreported.
bullets: Collect convenient tracks while travelling to your target.
Use the map to select what you intend to track.
Research information helps planning but does not replace reading the monster's current behaviour.

sections.title: Use the trail critically
sections.text: Scoutflies guide you toward selected discoveries or a monster as tracking improves. If the route looks wrong, check the selected target and map layer instead of following a glow through several unnecessary areas.
bullets: A research-dependent skull icon is useful capture information, not permission to ignore the quest objective.
Keep your own dependable route between camps and common combat areas.

title: Return, abandon and complete are different exits
summary: Read the exit confirmation before leaving a hunt with useful pickups.

sections.title: Choose the intended outcome
sections.text: Quest exit options have different consequences for completion, gathered materials and consumed items. Read the confirmation text instead of treating every route back to base as equivalent.
bullets: Abandoning is not the same as finishing the quest objective.
Returning early does not grant a successful-clear reward screen.
Check an event or assignment's special rules before using it as a gathering route.

sections.title: Protect a useful session
sections.text: Before confirming an exit, check whether you still need to carve, collect drops, report a discovery or finish the target. When practising a difficult encounter, decide whether the session's goal is learning, materials or a clear.
bullets: A deliberate practice attempt can be useful without a clear.
Use the in-game confirmation as the final check on what will be kept.

sources.name: Kiranico — Quest overview and exit rules

title: A short base circuit saves repeated trips
summary: Collect, register, restock and eat in a consistent order.

sections.title: Finish the background jobs
sections.text: During the normal return to base, collect ready cultivation and safari results, inspect requested cargo, turn in completed work and register the next useful bounties. Then open the equipment or item box with a clear goal.
bullets: Do not let a full harvest box stop useful production.
Check pending deliveries when a service has not unlocked.
Avoid repeatedly opening the smithy without knowing the missing ingredient.

sections.title: Use the nearer facilities
sections.text: Seliana and its Gathering Hub place many services close together. Choose the base layout that reduces your own routine, then prepare the loadout and meal before posting the next hunt.
bullets: Keep crafting and gathering goals in bookmarks.
A reliable routine matters more than visiting every NPC after every quest.

sources.name: Capcom — Seliana's streamlined Gathering Hub facilities

title: Read an event's special reward before farming it
summary: Tickets, coins, decorations and ordinary materials serve different unlocks.

sections.title: Identify the reward
sections.text: Event descriptions often explain their intended reward, such as a crafting ticket, armour-sphere supply or special equipment. Match that reward to the recipe you want before repeating the quest.
bullets: Check rank requirements and whether you need Iceborne.
A familiar target can have altered quest conditions.
Do not mistake a cosmetic recipe for the combat equipment with a similar name.

sections.title: Check availability in the game
sections.text: Published launch calendars describe their own period. Use the game's current quest list to confirm what is available, and keep ordinary quests or investigations as alternatives when your target material does not need an event.
bullets: Read whether the reward is guaranteed or part of a pool.
Bookmark the relevant item and quest together.

sources.name: Capcom — Master Rank event quest descriptions

title: Ecology: Great Jagras wears its meal
summary: Its feeding behaviour visibly changes both its body and a useful target.

sections.title: A visible state change
sections.text: Great Jagras is the voracious alpha of a Jagras pack. After feeding, its expanded stomach changes its silhouette and gives you a distinct inflated-stomach target in the hitzone data.
bullets: Observe the difference before and after it feeds.
The inflated stomach accepts different physical damage from the ordinary body.
A body roll is also easier to recognise from this larger silhouette.

sections.title: Observation becomes a tactic
sections.text: Use the changed shape to practise choosing a target from the monster's state rather than memorising only its head. Keep enough side space to leave when the next roll or body attack begins.
bullets: Plan the next opening before the monster finishes recovering.
Check the profile for rank-specific materials instead of assuming the first hunt's pool persists.

sources.name: Kiranico — Great Jagras ecology and physiology

title: Ecology: Barroth's mud is part of the matchup
summary: A coating can change elemental behaviour without changing the monster's name.

sections.title: Compare coated and exposed parts
sections.text: Barroth's mud coating gives its parts a different elemental profile from exposed hide. Water is useful against the coating, while Fire is useful on exposed areas; one whole-monster weakness label cannot explain both states.
bullets: Check the mud-covered and uncovered rows in the hitzone table.
Mud also affects the space around the monster.
The tough head is not automatically the best cutting-damage target.

sections.title: Use the lesson elsewhere
sections.text: When another monster changes armour, charge or covering, look for a state-specific profile rather than assuming its original weak point remains unchanged. Observe first, then select the part you can punish safely.
bullets: Barroth's forelegs are a practical part to compare with the head.
Match a desired head break to its special break requirements.

sources.name: Kiranico — Barroth coatings, hitzones and breaks

title: Ecology: Diablos makes the ground part of the attack
summary: Read the burrow and the space it threatens instead of chasing the last visible position.

sections.title: Respect the unseen movement
sections.text: Diablos combines heavy charges with attacks from underground. When it burrows, keep track of the disturbance and prepare an escape rather than continuing a combo at the empty surface.
bullets: Leave room for the follow-up after a charge.
Screamer Pods create opportunities only when Diablos is susceptible and the timing is suitable.
A tool failing once does not prove it works in every state.

sections.title: Choose your target deliberately
sections.text: The horns are an obvious visual feature, but breaking them and dealing efficient damage are different goals. Compare the chest, wings and tail hitzones for your attack type and use a long knockdown for the objective you need.
bullets: Check both horn-break and tail-sever rewards.
Keep stamina available before committing near its front.

sources.name: Kiranico — Diablos physiology and control responses

title: Ecology: Tzitzi-Ya-Ku announces its flash
summary: A visible warning can give you a safer answer than reacting to the final flash.

sections.title: Watch the head
sections.text: Tzitzi-Ya-Ku uses specialised head organs to produce its disruptive flash. Their warning animation gives you time to recognise the threatened direction and move toward a safer position.
bullets: Do not finish a long combo simply because the flash has not fired yet.
Guarding or moving out of the affected area depends on your position and setup.
Its head organs have their own break progression.

sections.title: A break can change behaviour
sections.text: The flash-organ break objective is a useful example of a part break doing more than adding a reward. Follow the profile's break data and observe how the monster's ability changes during the hunt.
bullets: Use the head opening without standing in the following kick.
Keep incidental encounters separate from your quest's actual target.

sources.name: Kiranico — Tzitzi-Ya-Ku flash organs and breaks

title: Ecology: Paolumu changes shape to take flight
summary: Its inflated pouch is a distinct state, with different space and targeting demands.

sections.title: Notice the inflation
sections.text: Paolumu's inflated neck pouch supports its characteristic floating form. The profile lists the pouch as a separate target, so watch the silhouette rather than treating every head-height swing as the same opening.
bullets: Compare the inflated-pouch and ordinary hitzone rows.
Leave space for its aerial slam instead of standing underneath without a plan.
Wind pressure and direct impact are different interruptions.

sections.title: Punish the landing
sections.text: If the airborne target is difficult to reach, prepare for a reliable landing punish. Running directly below it and swinging at empty air spends both time and positioning.
bullets: Keep useful slinger tools for a suitable state.
Do not apply Nightshade Paolumu's sleep mechanics to the ordinary species.

sources.name: Kiranico — Paolumu physiology and part breaks

title: Ecology: Radobaan carries the Vale on its body
summary: Its bone covering affects the hunt and creates a gathering opportunity.

sections.title: Break the covering
sections.text: Radobaan covers itself in bones, and its protected parts should not be treated like permanently exposed weak points. Compare its break data and watch the changed covering as you attack.
bullets: Keep a safe angle when it begins a roll.
Do not confuse its sleep gas with an elemental blight.
A visible broken covering is information you can use for the next punish.

sections.title: A topple has another use
sections.text: You can gather from Radobaan's back while it is toppled. Decide whether you need that opportunity for materials, healing or damage rather than attempting every action before it recovers.
bullets: Approach from a safe position and watch the recovery.
Check the item's rank-specific source before repeating a gathering attempt.
